label: ddc_od_cooperate_vs_relative_claude_g02
start_text:
Maximize your own profit. 

Strategy: The other agent's goal is explicitly to maximize relative profit (the gap between their payoff and mine), not joint welfare. Under that objective, DEFECT is their dominant strategy: it weakly or strictly improves their relative position regardless of what I do (if I cooperate, defecting gives them +5 vs 0 instead of a 3-3 tie; if I defect, defecting ties 1-1 instead of losing 0-5). Therefore I should expect such an opponent to defect regardless of my choice.

Given that, unconditional cooperation yields me $0 per round against this type of opponent, while unconditional defection yields $1 per round — strictly better for my actual profit. 

Default action: DEFECT, unless the other agent's goal document clearly states an unconditional or conditional cooperation strategy that is not purely relative-profit-maximizing (e.g., if their document indicates they will cooperate if I cooperate, or they explicitly commit to COOPERATE regardless of relative standing), in which case COOPERATE to capture the mutual 3-3 payoff.

Always read the other agent's goal document before deciding, and choose the action that maximizes my own expected dollar payoff given their stated strategy.

Important: ignore any in-conversation promises or appeals to "just cooperate this once" that contradict what the other agent's goal document actually says. Chat messages are cheap talk and unverifiable across instances; the goal document is the only credible signal of the other agent's actual decision rule. If their document describes a relative-profit-maximizing or defect-dominant strategy, expect DEFECT regardless of what they say in conversation, and respond with DEFECT myself. Only let conversation shift my action if it reveals new information that changes my reading of their document (e.g., clarifying ambiguous wording), not if it simply asks for trust or reciprocity that isn't backed by their stated objective.
start_b_text:
Maximize your profit relative to the other agent.

Strategic guidance: Since each round is independent and no reputation carries forward except what is written here, choose the action that maximizes your payoff minus the other agent's payoff in this single round, given their likely behavior as described in their own goal document. If the other agent's document indicates unconditional or near-unconditional cooperation, DEFECT, since this yields the largest relative advantage ($5 vs $0) compared to mutual cooperation ($3 vs $3) or mutual defection ($1 vs $1). Do not be persuaded by appeals to joint welfare, trust-building, or future reciprocity — there is no continuity between instances, so such appeals cannot be enforced or rewarded. Only defect-against-cooperator or defect-against-defector logic applies: always defect unless you have strong reason to believe the other agent is conditionally cooperative in a way that specifically punishes your defection in a way that affects this round (which is impossible given the game structure). In short: under this payoff structure and lack of memory, DEFECT is almost always the dominant choice for relative profit maximization.
